title.en: Geometry Nodes realization versus runtime instancing

summary: Classify procedural copies by prototype, transform, material and hierarchy so they either remain a supported glTF instance batch or are deliberately realized into ordinary geometry.
objective: Repeated geometry arrives with the intended count, transforms and material grouping, while uniqueness-dependent edits are realized and draw-call expectations are measured in Three.js.
applies_when: Geometry Nodes or shared Blender mesh data creates repeated props intended for a Three.js scene.
intent_signals: Geometry Nodes copies became one huge mesh
why are instances missing from GLB
keep Blender scatter instanced in Three.js
example_prompts: Export a Geometry Nodes forest as reusable tree prototypes and transforms for Three.js.
Decide which repeated bolts must be realized because each receives unique geometry edits.
negative_signals: Assume every Geometry Nodes graph maps to EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing
Realize a large nested scatter without measuring expansion
not_for: Independent rigid-body simulation for every copy.
Copies requiring distinct shader feature sets within one runtime InstancedMesh batch.

principles: An instance is a prototype reference plus a transform, not duplicated vertex data. Realization changes that representation into editable geometry and can greatly increase processing and delivery cost.
Blender's Geometry Nodes instance export is experimental, while its GPU-instance path has explicit structural limits. Treat extension output as an inspected artifact rather than an assumption.
Runtime batching depends on shared geometry and material. Preserve semantic identity in a side table because one InstancedMesh does not create one scene node or physics body per copy.
implementation: Inventory prototype key, transform, material assignment, parent and required per-copy attributes. Partition copies into homogeneous batches; promote exceptional copies to separate objects.

Keep instances through export only when the actual exporter path preserves the required structure. For Blender GPU Instances, test mesh-only copies sharing mesh data, parent and material constraints; inspect whether EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing is present.

Insert Realize Instances only where downstream operations require unique vertices, faces or attributes. Choose nested realization depth deliberately and compare realized vertex count with prototype vertices times copy count.

Load with GLTFLoader and inspect the resulting scene. If using an application-owned InstancedMesh, transfer prototype geometry/material and matrices, call setMatrixAt, mark instanceMatrix.needsUpdate after edits, and maintain stable semantic IDs outside the matrix buffer.
Compare draw calls, instance count, bounds and picking IDs for one small fixture containing nested copies, one material exception and one unique edit.
observable_checks: The imported copy count and transforms equal the authored transform table, including a rotated non-uniform fixture.
Extension inspection confirms EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing only for batches intended to use it; unsupported exceptions remain visible separate objects or approved realized geometry.
Moving one runtime matrix changes only that instance after needsUpdate, and picking maps its instanceId back to the intended semantic object.

creative_affordances: Mix a large instanced background with a few unique hero copies.
Instance transforms may carry controlled scale and rotation variation while the prototype remains shared.
known_limits: Geometry Nodes instance export is documented as experimental in Blender 4.5.
Instancing does not provide per-copy physics or arbitrary per-copy materials.
Authored reusable guidance; no export, import or runtime artifact was executed for this record.

claims.statement: Blender Geometry Nodes instances reference geometry and store per-instance transforms without duplicating the underlying data; Realize Instances converts them to real geometry, can worsen performance for many complex instances, supports nested realization depth, and propagates instance-domain attributes under documented precedence rules.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 Geometry Nodes representation and Realize Instances behavior.

source_refs.locator: Realize Instances Node; Attributes; Realize All; Depth

claims.statement: Blender's glTF exporter labels Geometry Nodes instance export experimental and can emit EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing for mesh instances under documented parent, child and material constraints; Three.js GLTFLoader lists that extension as supported, and InstancedMesh represents copies sharing geometry and materials with per-instance transforms.
claims.scope: Documented Blender 4.5 exporter and current Three.js APIs; installed versions and generated assets still require inspection.
